Order
22.03.2023 Order No.
Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner and learned counsel for the State.

2. The Petitioner is an accused in G.R. Case No.504 of 2022 pending on the file of learned NGN,
Puri arising out of Puri Sadar P.S. Case No.270 of 2022 for commission of the alleged offence under Sections 341/323/376(2)(n)/313/506 of I.P.C.
3.

entities.text: Puri Sadar P.S. Case No.270 of 2022
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Being aggrieved by the rejection of his application for bail U/s. 439 Cr.P.C by the learned 2nd Addl. Sessions Judge, Puri by order dated 26.12.2022 in the aforementioned case, the present BLAPL has been filed.

4. It is submitted by the learned counsel that the Petitioner is in custody since 03.12.2022 and as preliminary charge sheet has already been filed on 14.12.2022, further continuance of the Petitioner in custody is not warranted.
5.
Learned counsel for the State and the Informant oppose the prayer for bail.

6. Learned counsel for the Informant places on record the order of this Court dated 8.2.2023 passed in CRLMP No.2112 of 2022 and the order dated 16.3.2023 passed in I.A. No.85 of 2023 arising out of the said CRLMP.
7.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the Informant that being aggrieved by the deletion of Umakanta Rath @ Raja vs State Of Odisha & Another .... Opposite ... on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89391985/
1 the offences under the I.T Act and IPC, the Petitioner approached this Court and by order dated 8.2.2023 referred to hereinabove this Court directed the I.I.C., Puri Sadar Police Station to re-investigate the matter and add the offence under the Indian Penal Code, if it is prima facie made out.

entities.text: Umakanta Rath @ Raja vs State Of Odisha & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, it is submitted that if the Petitioner is released at this stage, the order of this Court in CRLMP No.2112 of 2022 shall be frustrated.
8. Learned counsel for the Petitioner submits that the order in the CRLMP was passed without notice to the accused.
9. Learned counsel for the Informant fairly submits that the accused was not impleaded in the said CRLMP.

10. Operative paragraph of the order dated 08.02.2023 in CRLMP No.2112 of 2022 of this Court is extracted hereunder:
"xxx xxx xxx 5.

Keeping in view the above facts and circumstances made, the I.I.C., Kumbarpara Police Station (opposite party no.3) is directed to reinvestigate the matter in connection with the above noted P.S.
Case and add the offence under the Indian Penal Code if it is prima facie made out and communicate it to the learned S.D.J.M., Puri to look into the charges and consider the prayer for amending the Sections, if necessary, under which the F.I.R. has been registered...."

11. It is apt to state that the name of the Police Station has been modified as "IIC, Puri Sadar P.S." in terms of the order dated 16.03.2023 passed in I.A. No.85 of 2023 arising out of the said CRLMP No.2112 of 2022.

12. This Court is not persuaded to accept contention of the learned counsel for the Informant that in view of the order passed in CRLMP No.2112 of 2022, the Petitioner ought not to be released on bail,
on perusal of the statement of the victim under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
13.

Considering the tenor thereof and filing of the preliminary charge sheet and the period of pre-trial detention, this Court directs the Petitioner to be released on bail on such terms to be fixed by the learned court in seisin.
14. Additionally, it is directed that the Petitioner shall cooperate with the investigation.
The Informant may seek variance of this order in the event there is any threat perception.
15. The BLAPL accordingly stands disposed of.
16. Urgent certified copy of this order be granted as per rule.
(V. NARASINGH) Judge PKS Umakanta Rath @ Raja vs State Of Odisha & Another ....
